paragraphs: Mar Zutra, Rav Ashi’s colleague. He smelled King Azgor’s cooked dish, and Rav Ashi placed some in his mouth. The king’s officers told Rav Ashi he had spoiled the king’s food. Rav Ashi said this food was unfit for the king because it contained leprosy. They examined it and found leprosy in that piece, for a miracle was performed for him. He relied on the miracle because a leprous spirit had spread over Mar Zutra: Ketubbot 61b. When he went up to bed, he said, “Forgiven be whoever has distressed me”: Megillah 28a. (Sefer Zikhron Torat Moshe, entry forgiveness, writes that sleep is a sixtieth of death [ששים in source], and one should examine one’s deeds.) Yuchasin attributes this to Mar Zutra son of Rav Nachman. His burial is in Kefar Baram (G.A.Y.). Rav Acha son of Rav Yosef in his name. Rav Acha bar Yeiva reported him. He, Amemar and Rav Ashi were eating: Berakhot 44b. Rav Ashi said, “Mar Zutra told me”; Rav Chanina of Sura questions it: Menachot 31a; Niddah 52a. He visited Rav Ashi’s house: Berakhot 26a. Rav Gamda, Amemar and Rav Zevid (see his entry). In Rav Huna’s name: end of Bakhol Mearvin and Taanit 18b. Mar Zutra expounded in Mar Zutra Rabbah’s name. He expounded in Rav Chisda’s name: Ellu Terefot 44b. He acquired the property of Yehudah the Indian, who converted. Rav Yeimar and Merimar said; he attended Rabbi Pinchas son of Rabbi Ammi’s lecture (see his entry). Rav Yeimar bar Shizva said to him. He objects to Rav Mesharshya. In Rav Pappa’s name: Bava Metzia 67b; Chullin 43a. “I saw Rav Pappi.” He visited Rava bar Chinena; and Rabbah bar Safra. In Rav Sheshet’s name: Bekhorot 27b. Tosafot and Rosh, Bava Metzia chapter 1, say the law follows Rav Ashi against Mar Zutra. Mar Zutra ruled eight years (see part 1, year 4162).
